items.prompt: A DeskPilot ticket is closed. Which statuses may it transition to?
items.answer: Only in_progress: a closed ticket can be reopened, nothing else
distractors: None: closed is a terminal status, so every transition is refused
open or in_progress, so a reopened ticket can go back to the queue
Any status except closed itself, as long as the ticket is not merged
items.explanation: rules.closed is ["in_progress"]: not resolved, blocked or open. Note that nothing anywhere transitions back to open; open only appears as a starting status.

items.prompt: transitionTicket is asked to move a blocked ticket to blocked. What happens?
items.answer: The ticket is returned unchanged, with no write and no status_changed event
distractors: A TransitionError, because blocked is not in blocked's own allowed list
The ticket is rewritten and a blocked -> blocked status_changed event is logged
The ticket's updatedAt is bumped and saved, but no status event is logged
items.explanation: The same-status check returns early, before the rules lookup, so idempotent requests are harmless.

items.prompt: What happens to a ticket that has been merged into another one?
items.answer: It can no longer transition, and listTickets hides it from the list
distractors: It transitions together with the ticket it was merged into from then on
It is deleted from the JSON store at merge time, leaving only the target
It can still transition, but only to closed, and stays in the ticket list
items.explanation: transitionTicket rejects isMerged tickets with TransitionError 'Merged tickets cannot transition.', and listTickets filters out ticket.isMerged. The record stays in the store, pointing at mergedIntoId.

items.prompt: Two createTicket calls for the same org run concurrently. Both readDb before either writes. What can the stored file end up with?
items.answer: Only one ticket: each writes its own full copy, so the later write erases the other
distractors: Both tickets, because writeQueue serializes the two read-modify-write cycles
Both tickets, sharing one ticketNumber, but nothing is lost from the file itself
Neither ticket, because the second write detects the conflict and both abort
items.explanation: writeQueue only orders the writeFile calls; the read-modify-write cycle around them is not serialized. Each caller serializes the whole db object it read, so the second write replaces the first (and both computed the same ticketNumber).

items.prompt: A successful transitionTicket call: how many readDb and writeDb calls does it make in total?
items.answer: 3 readDb and 2 writeDb, one read-modify-write per store function
distractors: 1 readDb and 1 writeDb, wrapped together in a single transaction
2 readDb and 1 writeDb, since the status and event share one write
3 readDb and 3 writeDb, since every store function writes the file
items.explanation: getTicketById, setTicketStatus and addTransitionEvent each read the whole database; the last two each write it back. The status change and its event are separate writes, so a failure between them leaves a status change with no audit event.

items.prompt: A resolved ticket is reopened (resolved -> in_progress). What happens to its resolvedAt?
items.answer: It keeps the old timestamp, since reopening never clears resolvedAt
distractors: It is cleared to null, since the ticket is no longer resolved
It is set to the reopen time, like updatedAt on every status change
It is moved into a reopenedAt field and resolvedAt is left empty
items.explanation: setTicketStatus only assigns resolvedAt when the new status is resolved or closed; there is no branch that resets it, so reports can show an in-progress ticket as resolved.

items.prompt: On a new ticket, an agent first adds an internal note, then a customer comments, then the agent replies publicly. Which comment sets firstResponseAt?
items.answer: The agent's public reply, the first comment that is both agent and public
distractors: The internal note, since it is the first comment written by an agent
The customer's comment, since it is the first public comment on the ticket
None: firstResponseAt is set only by a transition out of the open status
items.explanation: The condition is !ticket.firstResponseAt && authorType === "agent" && !isInternal: internal notes and customer comments never count. It is set once and never moved.

items.prompt: A comment body is  Tom & Jerry <b>  . What bodyHtml is stored?
items.answer:
Tom & Jerry <b>

: trimmed, and only the < and > are escaped
distractors:
Tom & Jerry <b>

: trimmed, with every HTML special escaped

Tom & Jerry

: stored exactly as sent, with nothing escaped

Tom & Jerry

: trimmed, with only the ampersand escaped
items.explanation: bodyHtml is built with replaceAll("<", "<").replaceAll(">", ">") on the trimmed body. Ampersands and quotes pass through untouched.

items.prompt: updateTicketFields is called with exactly the ticket's current subject and priority. What changes?
items.answer: updatedAt is bumped and the file rewritten, but no ticket.updated event is logged
distractors: Nothing at all: the function compares the fields and returns before writing
updatedAt is bumped and a ticket.updated event with no changed fields is logged
A validation error is thrown, because an update must change at least one field
items.explanation: updatedAt = nowIso() runs unconditionally; the event push is guarded by Object.keys(newValue).length > 0. The ticket jumps to the top of the updatedAt-sorted list anyway.

items.prompt: updateTicketFields receives tags [" vip", "vip", "", "billing"]. What does the ticket store?
items.answer: ["vip", "billing"]: trimmed, empties dropped, deduplicated in order
distractors: [" vip", "vip", "billing"]: only the empty tag is dropped before saving
["billing", "vip"]: trimmed, empties dropped, then deduplicated and sorted
[" vip", "vip", "", "billing"]: tags are stored exactly as they were sent
items.explanation: Array.from(new Set(tags.map(trim).filter(Boolean))) - a Set keeps first-seen insertion order. The event is only logged if the JSON of the new list differs from the old one.

items.prompt: Org A has tickets numbered 1-7 and org B has 1-30. What ticketNumber does org A's next ticket get?
items.answer: 8: the next number is org A's own maximum plus one
distractors: 31: numbers are shared across orgs, so it follows 30
38: the total ticket count across both orgs plus one
A UUID-derived number, so numbers never collide
items.explanation: nextTicketNumber filters to the org and reduces with Math.max starting at 0, so it is the per-org maximum plus one.

items.front: What does the writeQueue promise chain in store.ts guarantee, and what does it not?
items.back: It guarantees writeFile calls never overlap (no interleaved, corrupt JSON). It does not serialize read-modify-write cycles, so concurrent updates can still overwrite each other.

items.front: How does getTimeline build a ticket's timeline?
items.back: It maps comments and ticket events into one tagged union (kind: comment | event), concatenates them, and sorts by createdAt ascending with localeCompare on ISO strings.

items.front: What does parseNonEmptyString(value) return for a number, for "   ", and for "  hi  "?
items.back: null for a non-string; null for whitespace-only (trimmed length below min 1); "hi" trimmed for a valid string (max length 500 by default).
